links.comparator_used: Six human clinicians evaluating responses to Rwandan health workers' questions (five LLM judges compared against them)
links.outcome: Agreement of LLM judges with human clinician ratings across 11 evaluation criteria
links.effect: Best LLM judge (Claude-4.1-Opus) matched human evaluators on only 4 of 11 criteria; Gemini-2.5-Pro scored too leniently and GPT-5 too harshly
links.tradeoff: Performance and cost-effectiveness fell when moving from English to Kinyarwanda
links.quote: The highest-performing LLM-judge (Claude-4.1-Opus) matched human evaluators on only four of eleven evaluation criteria, with other models scoring too leniently (Gemini-2.5-Pro) or too harshly (GPT-5).

links.comparator_used: Individual LLM judges / single-model LLM-as-judge evaluations
links.outcome: Agreement with human evaluators across evaluation criteria
links.effect: LLM-juries improved agreement on only one additional criterion.
links.quote: Constructing LLM-juries to balance model-specific biases improved agreement on only one additional criterion.

design_hint: LLM-as-judge evaluation vs human clinician review of outputs
